1. Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day forecast horizon — adjust upward by 2–5% for the first 5–7 days.

2. Model exhibits strong upward bias after sharp price spikes (e.g., 80+ → 90+), often overshooting the true peak — cap forecast at 10% above the immediate prior peak or use moving average of recent 5-day highs.

3. Model fails to capture mean reversion in the latter half of the forecast — true prices often dip after initial spikes — apply a downward correction of 1–3% for days 20–30 if prior 5-day average was above 90.

4. Forecast lags true price movements by 1–3 days — adjust forecast by adding 1–2% per day for lagged price increases (e.g., if true price rises 2% on day 5, forecast should be 2.2–2.4% higher on day 6).

5. Model overfits to recent low prices — when history includes a recent dip, forecast should not be overly optimistic — use 30-day rolling median as a floor for forecast, especially if true price rebounds sharply.
